Refreshed Honda Accord e:HEV Gets $1,000 Pricier in Australia for 2027
9 photos
Photo: Honda
Priced AUD 1,000 higher than its predecessor, the 2027 Honda Accord e:HEV is barely different from the 2026 model when you analyze their specification sheets side by side. The Japanese automaker has tidied up a few choice exterior details, added some red stitching for good measure, cut the complimentary Honda Connect subscription from 5 to 3 years, and that's pretty much it.
Honda's Aussie subsidiary couldn't make a case for any powertrain updates, and there is no additional standard kit to soften the price increase either, leaving the Accord between a rock and a hard place. The 2027 model does little to give prospective customers a fresh reason to choose it over the Toyota Camry, which is exclusively four-pot hybrid in the Australian market since 2024.
Even its stylistic updates are hard to notice unless you park the 2027 Accord right next to its forerunner. Honda started by replacing the gloss-black lower body trim pieces and headlight surrounds with body-color trim. A black insert now occupies the lower front bumper where silver trim used to sit, and the amber reflectors of the front lighting units have disappeared for a cleaner aesthetic.
Honda further deleted the blue outlines previously used on the exterior badges, yet the e:HEV lettering that designates the hybrid four-cylinder powertrain remains on the trunk lid. Hopping inside, the biggest difference over the 2026 and earlier models is the adoption of red stitching throughout the cabin. The infotainment system and other equipment otherwise carry over.
That means Accord buyers are presented with a 10.2-inch digital instrument cluster, an 11.5-inch HUD, 12.3 inches of central infotainment touchscreen, and 12 audio speakers from Bose. A panoramic sunroof, 360-degree cameras, and cordless Apple CarPlay plus Android Auto remain standard. Heated front seats are notably absent, which is ridiculous when smaller and cheaper vehicles now come with heating in the front seats by default.
Photo: Honda Given the drive-away price of nearly AUD 66,000 before options, that omission is definitely uncomfortable. Honda Australia has essentially increased the starting price without giving the mid-sized sedan a standard feature that would make those additional AUD 1,000 easier to justify against the Camry and similar vehicles.
And that's not all, though, for Honda Australia has nerfed the Honda Connect complimentary subscription by 2 years. The service handles a number of remote functions, including remote locking and unlocking, climate control, location information, and vehicle status. All things considered, the Accord e:HEV is clearly moving in the wrong direction for 2027.
The bad news continues with Honda Australia's low-price scheduled servicing, which now costs AUD 279 per visit instead of AUD 199 prior to October 2026. That increase is separate from the Accord's 2027 facelift , but forms part of the ownership arithmetic for anyone looking at a brand-new Accord today. Under the hood, a familiar 2.0-liter naturally aspirated I4 hybrid soldiers on with 135 kW (181 hp) and 335 Nm (247 lb-ft) on tap.
Per the attached specifications sheet, the front-drive sedan drinks 4.3 liters per 100 kilometers (54.7 miles per gallon US) in the combined test cycle, based on the ADR 81/02 testing procedure. Undoubtedly respectable by mid-size sedan standards, but still 0.3 liters off the Camry, which is hardly a surprise when you remember that Toyota has the more efficient internal combustion engine and hybrid system to boot.
